column1: # Tranquility builds and how long the server lagged each one (docs/guides/tracking-tq.md,
# "Metrics"). Build numbers, lines and UTC times only; no client data. Written by
# `python3 -I tools/tq-lag.py --record STEP BUILD`; `-` is a step not reached.
#   tier        T0 data only, T1 code change, T2 new line, T3 native protocol change (or -)
#   seen_by     notes, esi, launcher or report: the source that showed the build first
#   note        an [A] with its falsifier for every time that is not proved
# Evidence for the seed rows: tools/builds.tsv (evidence column), the import time in
# out/new-build/<build>/import.txt [V] and the git log of the re-pin commit [V].

column12: [A] seen_utc is the import time (import.txt, proved), so the lag is a lower bound; falsifier: ESI or notes history shows the build deployed earlier. [A] served_utc is the re-pin commit time (git log, proved), not the deploy; falsifier: the stack log shows the build accepted at another time. T0 is [I] from builds.tsv (data-only delta)
